requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
## Judgment

The storage implementation substantially fulfills `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`, but required tests are not fully traced to this requirement. No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges these gaps.

## Obligations and implementation

The requirement imposes these separate obligations:

1. Give each assessment a separate usage record.
2. Store it as JSON.
3. Use `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`.
4. Apply `requirements.configuration.state_location` to usage storage.
5. Identify the format version.
6. Identify the run.
7. Identify the project root.
8. Identify the subject kind.
9. Identify the subject's full name.
10. Identify the start time.
11. Identify the backend when known.
12. Identify the model when known.
13. Identify the end time when finished.
14. Identify the outcome.
15. Identify the accepted determination kind when present.
16. Identify whether evidence was written.
17. Record the selected `file` or `stdout` destination in `evidence_output`.
18. Mark a successful file write as `evidence_written: true`.
19. Mark a successful stdout write as `evidence_written: true`.
20. Keep stdout-mode usage recording outside the project.
21. Exclude FIXME entry text.
22. Distinguish failed runs from completed judgments.
23. Distinguish cancelled runs from completed judgments.
24. Distinguish unfinished runs from completed judgments.
25. Persist records for later review.
26. Exclude source text.
27. Exclude prompts.
28. Exclude responses.
29. Exclude rationale.

### Record creation, location, and identity (1–14, 25)

`src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_output]` reaches `author_evidence_with_options`, `usage_state_root`, and `UsageLog::start`. The batch root `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]` also reaches them. `src/authoring/usage.rs#impl[UsageLog]/fn[start]` creates a uniquely named file, initializes identifying metadata and an unfinished outcome, and saves JSON; `impl[UsageLog]/fn[save]` writes the persistent record. `impl[UsageLog]/fn[finish]` records the final outcome and end time.

`src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[usage_state_root]` applies the cited state-location requirement through `src/config.rs#fn[state_root]` and `fn[state_root_from]`, rejects project-contained state through `fn[state_in_project]`, and creates the state directory. This reviews the subject's application of state-location behavior, not that cited requirement independently.

Metadata is completed by `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]`, `fn[backend_name]`, and `fn[assess_subject]`. The marked test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` checks JSON naming, location, version, run ID, canonical project root, subject name and kind, backend, model, and timestamps, as well as unavailable state. `fn[usage_record_of_an_early_failure_identifies_its_subject_kind]` checks early-failure metadata. `fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` checks the selected model; `fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` checks Bedrock identity. Batch record separation and persistence across invocations are exercised by `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]`.

There is also a separate conditional creation path: `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess_subject]` calls `fn[followup_log]` for independent confirmation and verification conversations. The test-reference gap for this path is listed below.

### Determination, destination, and successful writes (15–20)

`src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess]` stores only `Judgment::kind()` in usage; `fn[assess_subject]` updates that kind when verification changes the selected result. `fn[author_evidence_with_options]` sets the selected destination. `fn[configured_assessment]` sets `evidence_written` after successful file or stdout writing; `impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]` does so for batch persistence.

Marked tests `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]`, `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, and `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` cover determination kinds and successful destinations. `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` checks absent accepted determinations and unwritten evidence. `fn[failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage]` checks that an accepted kind survives an evidence-write failure. `fn[usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it]` explicitly checks the outside-project constraint in stdout mode as well as file mode.

### Failure classification (22–24)

`src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]`, `fn[prepare_assessment]`, and `impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[failed]` distinguish interrupted cancellation from failure and completion. Initial records remain unfinished until finalized. Marked tests `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` and `fn[interrupted_terminal_progress_keeps_unstarted_work_incomplete]` assert failed and cancelled outcomes; the latter reaches `fn[assert_interruption_stops_the_batch]`. `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cancelled_request_persists_elapsed_time_and_incomplete_totals]` asserts the initially unfinished outcome, absent initial end time, and cancelled final state.

### Content exclusion (21, 26–29)

`src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]` and its serialized metadata types have no source, prompt, response, rationale, or FIXME-entry payload fields. `impl[UsageLog]/fn[prepared]` reduces input text to metadata rather than serializing it; determination storage reduces judgments to their kinds. Marked tests `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[input_metadata_counts_components_and_reads_without_persisting_source]` and `mod[tests]/fn[tool_outcomes_are_distinct_and_unknown_names_do_not_leak_model_text]` check exclusions. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` additionally checks that source, requirement, definition, rationale, and FIXME issue text delivered in the conversation do not appear in usage.

## Gaps

- **Separate follow-up records lack the required test reference.** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]` runs the conditional `followup_log` path and asserts that the independent second assessment has its own stored usage record. It carries only `{test}` for `requirements.authoring.confirmation`, not `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`. The marked usage-storage batch tests supplied here do not assert this separate confirmation-record path. This test needs a `{test}` reference to the subject.
- **The OpenAI backend-identification test lacks the required test reference.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[backend_name]` has a distinct OpenAI output path. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` exercises it and asserts `usage["backend"] == "openai"`, but references provider, mapping, usage-request, and configuration-storage requirements only. It needs a `{test}` reference to `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` for this governed output path. The subject-marked backend tests cover Ollama and Bedrock, not this path.

Both tests were located by searching beyond the subject's referenced tests. Under the task's explicit test-traceability rule, their existence without the subject reference does not close these gaps.

text: :::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
:::{req} policy
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`confirm`. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment, whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
